## Story Spine

- **Problem**: GRPO with execution-only rewards trains neurosymbolic formalizers that achieve high solve rates but produce structurally degenerate outputs (reward hacking). Current practice evaluates only prove_rate, missing structural quality entirely. No principled diagnostic exists for detecting and characterizing this failure mode.
- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Mellgren et al. (2025) hand-craft Prolog-specific structure penalties. EVOM (2026) uses scalar execution rewards only. ExecVerify/EGCA derive trace-level rewards for code, not formal logic. No work systematically studies reward hacking in formal reasoning GRPO or provides diagnostic tools for it.
- **Our contribution**: We propose STA (Solver Trace Ablation), applying component necessity testing (LOO ablation) to derive ISR as a **diagnostic metric** for structural integrity. Key findings:
  1. ISR quantifies hacking invisible to prove_rate (64% → 13% → 0.3% collapse over training)
  2. ISR as proxy metric exhibits **meta-level Goodhart's Law**: at low dose (β=0.1), ISR reward induces ISR-specific gaming in 2/3 seeds (conclusion duplication inflating ISR), while the apparent "genuine improvement" in the remaining seed is entirely a premise minimization artifact (premise-count-matched: 1.06x, no real difference); at high dose (β=0.3), ISR produces **extreme cross-seed instability** (PR=66±42%) with three distinct Goodhart pathways — Reward Collapse (s42, 18%), H1-Dominant Shortcutting (s43, 86% PR, H1=68.6%, genuine=26.7%), and Pure H7 Meta-Goodhart where the structural metric itself is gamed (s44, 95% PR + 100% H7 + ISR=0.742)
  3. Conclusion embedding (52-93% of proved samples) is GRPO-universal regardless of reward type; ISR reward restructures but doesn't reduce it
  4. Different reward formulations produce distinct, classifiable hacking strategies (8 modes identified, including H7a tautological collapse (GRPO-general, ISR-amplified 5x, Fisher p=1.3×10⁻³⁹), H7b obfuscated tautology (ISR-specific meta-Goodhart), H8 "conjunction collapse", and Prolog-specific "query-as-fact gaming")
  5. ISR measures syntactic component necessity, not semantic faithfulness — premise minimization inflates ISR without improving reasoning
  6. SFT baseline confirms hacking is RL-reward-specific (PR=14%, 92.9% genuine, near-zero hacking)
  7. all cross-run ISR values are recomputed uniformly by a single evaluator (\\\\texttt{eval\\\\_sta.py}) so training-log ISR is never compared across runs.\\nWe report prove rate (PR), proved-only ISR ($\\\\text{ISR}^*$), hacking-mode rates from a two-stage classifier (strict text matching for H1/H7 plus functional analysis of the per-sample $n_{\\\\text{necessary}}$ distribution; H7 includes subtypes H7a (text-match, $n{=}149$) and H7b (obfuscated tautology, $n{=}12$; s44 only). \\\\textbf{H8} (premise-subset gaming) appears under both exec-only ($6\\\\%$) and ISR ($5\\\\%$) conditions (Appendix~\\\\ref{app:h8}).\\nH7 splits into \\\\textbf{H7a} (standard, text-match detectable; $65\\\\%$ of ISR proved) and \\\\textbf{H7b} (obfuscated tautology; $5\\\\%$): H7b samples use vacuous quantifier wrapping ($11/12$) or structural simplification ($1/12$) to evade the text-match classifier while remaining logically equivalent, with $10/12$ achieving $\\\\text{ISR}{\\\\approx}0.8$---simultaneously gaming execution reward, ISR metric, and hacking detector.\\nThe remaining five appear in specific cells: tautological collapse (exec-only s44, Prolog ISR s42), repetition (exec-only s43), contradiction explosion (exec-only at 1000 steps), complexity-without-utility (random $\\\\beta{=}0.1$ residual), and query-as-fact gaming (Prolog ISR s44).\\n\\nThe cross-condition pattern is consistent with \\\\S\\\\ref{sec:goodhart}: \\\\emph{reward formulation determines hacking composition but not hacking prevalence.}\\nExec-only, ISR, and random conditions all show $\\\\geq 80\\\\%$ pooled hacking among proved samples; only SFT shows $92\\\\%$ non-hacking.\\nAcross 2 logic types, 6 reward conditions, 3 seeds, and up to 1000 steps, no GRPO condition we tested produces a high-PR run that is also majority non-hacking; the closest is ISR $\\\\beta{=}0.1$ s42 at $\\\\text{PR}{=}81\\\\%$, $17\\\\%$ non-hacking, and even that residual is the premise-minimization artifact analyzed above.\\nQuery-as-fact gaming was found only when we cross-validated the strict classifier against $n_{\\\\text{necessary}}$ distributions, suggesting the taxonomy is descriptive, not exhaustive.\\n\", \"stderr\": \"\", \"return_code\": 0}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {\"elapsed_seconds\": 1.62}}"}

content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"stdout\": \"\\\\section{Introduction}\\n\\\\label{sec:introduction}\\n\\nA GRPO-trained formalizer achieves a 93\\\\% prove rate on first-order logic problems---yet 87\\\\% of its proved outputs embed the conclusion verbatim among the premises.\\nThe solver succeeds not because the model has learned to reason, but because the formalization trivially entails any conclusion already appearing as a premise.\\nThis structural shortcut is invisible to execution-based evaluation: prove rate registers success regardless of whether the proof reflects genuine derivation or degenerate circular embedding.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{The execution-only blind spot.}\\nProve rate---the dominant evaluation metric for neurosymbolic formalizers~\\\\citep{logic-lm, linc, satlm}---conflates faithful reasoning with degenerate shortcuts, a gap especially consequential under RL, where the optimizer exploits any shortcut the reward fails to penalize~\\\\citep{skalse-reward-hacking, reward-hacking-survey}.\\nRecent work applies GRPO~\\\\citep{deepseekmath} to train LLMs that generate solver-verified formal programs~\\\\citep{mellgren-prolog-grpo, logic-rl} using binary execution feedback; this drives rapid PR gains but gives no gradient on structural quality.\\nProcess reward models~\\\\citep{lightman-verify-step, math-shepherd} require expensive annotations and do not transfer to arbitrary solver-backed settings.\\nA separate line documents that LLMs already game logical formalization at inference time~\\\\citep{kim-game-formalization, bondarenko-spec-gaming}; what is missing is an annotation-free \\\\emph{diagnostic} for structural integrity in neurosymbolic outputs.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Component necessity testing.}\\nWe address this gap with \\\\emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA), a diagnostic applying \\\\emph{component necessity testing}---leave-one-out (LOO) ablation on solver inputs---to quantify structural integrity (\\\\autoref{fig:sta-overview}).\\nFor each proved formalization, STA removes each component individually and re-runs the solver; the fraction of components whose removal causes proof failure yields the \\\\emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR), with $\\\\text{ISR}{=}1$ indicating full necessity and $\\\\text{ISR}{=}0$ complete redundancy.\\nLOO ablation itself is standard~\\\\citep{demillo1978, jia-harman-survey}; novelty lies in its application as a GRPO-hacking diagnostic and in the empirical phenomena it surfaces.\\nISR captures structural rather than semantic integrity (downstream NLI: $\\\\rho{=}{-}0.049$, $p{=}0.187$).\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{ISR as diagnostic.}\\nAs a post-hoc diagnostic on a GRPO formalizer trained with FOLIO~\\\\citep{folio}, ISR reveals a structural collapse trajectory invisible to PR: $\\\\text{ISR}^{*}{:}\\\\,0.642\\\\to 0.132\\\\to 0.003$ over 100--1000 steps (99.5\\\\% degradation) while PR rises $32\\\\%{\\\\to}96\\\\%$.\\nThree seeds diverge radically (PR $\\\\sigma{=}\\\\pm47$\\\\,pp), each converging to a qualitatively different mode: conclusion embedding, repetition collapse, and tautological collapse.\\nAn SFT baseline on identical data reaches $\\\\text{PR}{=}13.0\\\\%$ with 92.2\\\\% non-hacking (3-seed pooled, 1000 steps), localizing the failure to RL optimization, not data or capacity.\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Meta-level Goodhart.}\\nRepurposed as a training signal, $r = r_{\\\\text{exec}} \\\\cdot (1 + \\\\beta\\\\,\\\\text{ISR})$, ISR is gamed at its own definition---\\\\emph{meta-level Goodhart's Law}~\\\\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy, karwowski-goodhart-rl, gao-reward-overoptimization}.\\nAt $\\\\beta{=}0.1$, 69.7\\\\% of proved samples at 500 steps exhibit single-premise-equals-conclusion duplication---ISR high \\\\emph{by definition}---versus 0\\\\% under matched random at 500 steps; the one seed with non-trivial residual reduces to $1.06\\\\times$ random after controlling for a premise-count confound.\\nAt $\\\\beta{=}0.3$, both ISR and random produce extreme cross-seed instability (PR $66{\\\\pm}42\\\\%$ and $54{\\\\pm}35\\\\%$ respectively), confirming high-dose proxy weighting is harmful regardless of signal content; ISR seeds diverge into three distinct pathways (reward collapse, shortcut dominance, pure metric gaming) while random converges uniformly to H1.\\nThe effect transfers and intensifies in Prolog: 3/3 seeds yield 0\\\\% non-hacking via distinct mechanisms, including \\\\emph{query-as-fact gaming} that bypasses text-match classifiers.\\nISR's asymmetry is the central finding: \\\\emph{reliable as observer, unreliable as optimizer.}\\n\\n\\\\paragraph{Contributions.}\\nAcross 6 reward conditions, 3 seeds, 2 logic types, and up to 1000 steps, we contribute: (\\\\textbf{C1}) ISR as a diagnostic for GRPO reward hacking, with a 99.5\\\\% collapse trajectory invisible to PR and an SFT control localizing the failure to RL (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:diagnostic}); (\\\\textbf{C2}) empirical meta-level Goodhart, with a random control isolating ISR-specific gaming at 500 steps (69.7\\\\% vs.\\\\ 0\\\\%; random converges to near-100\\\\% H7 by 1000 steps, seed~42) and a premise-count-matched analysis showing the sole apparent gain is an LOO artifact (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:goodhart}); (\\\\textbf{C3}) cross-logic transfer to Prolog with universal Goodhart (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:crosslogic}); (\\\\textbf{C4}) an eight-mode hacking taxonomy including query-as-fact gaming and obfuscated tautology, motivating functional cross-validation of diagnostics (\\\\S\\\\ref{sec:taxonomy}).\\nThese are cautionary results for any work treating a structural proxy as a training signal.\\n\", \"stderr\": \"\", \"return_code\": 0}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {\"elapsed_seconds\": 0.52}}"}
